exposure: Prenatal factors (cesarean delivery, pregnancy complications, smoking, breastfeeding duration)
cohort: 1,562 children and adolescents aged 6-17 years and their mothers in southern Brazil
finding: Cesarean delivery, pregnancy complications, and higher birth weight were positively associated with offspring BMI, while breastfeeding for 4-6 months was inversely associated.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery had a positive interaction with maternal BMI, leading to higher offspring BMI.
birth_weight: Low birth weight, normal birth weight, overweight
